title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
part: Part 14: Computer Science and Software Engineering
thesis: Master distributed systems, storage engines, consensus, replication, and scalability to dominate tier-1 software architecture.

chapters.name: Reliability, Scalability & Maintainability
chapters.detail: Measuring latency percentiles (p99, p99.9), handling load, and decoupling systems.

chapters.name: Data Models & Query Languages
chapters.detail: Relational vs Document vs Graph models: understanding when schemas-on-read vs schemas-on-write excel.

chapters.name: Storage & Retrieval
chapters.detail: LSM-Trees vs B-Trees, write-ahead logs, and indexes under the hood.

chapters.name: Distributed Data & Replication
chapters.detail: Leader-follower replication, split-brain syndromes, quorum reads, and eventual consistency.

chapters.name: Transactions & Consensus
chapters.detail: ACID vs BASE, serializability, two-phase commits, Paxos/Raft consensus algorithms.

mentalModels: Read Uncommitted to Serializable Isolation Levels
rules: Master distributed systems trade-offs to dominate senior/staff engineering interviews.
Always design systems expecting hardware failures, network partitions, and clock drift.
Think in p99 latencies and data durability rather than happy-path functionality.

title: The Millionaire Fastlane
author: MJ DeMarco
part: Part 27: The Fastlane & Unscripted Wealth Creation (FIRE Architecture)
thesis: Escape the 40-year Slowlane. Wealth is built through the Law of Effection, CENTS framework, and decoupled systems.

chapters.name: The Three Roads
chapters.detail: The Sidewalk (living paycheck to paycheck), The Slowlane (trading 5 days of freedom for 2 days of weekend for 40 years), The Fastlane (building scalable business systems).

chapters.name: The Law of Effection
chapters.detail: The more lives you affect in scale or magnitude, the wealthier you become. Wealth = Net Profit + Asset Value.

chapters.name: The CENTS Framework
chapters.detail: A Fastlane business must satisfy: Control, Entry (high barrier), Need, Time (detached from your hours), Scale.

chapters.name: Building Money Trees
chapters.detail: Rental systems, computer/software systems, content systems, distribution systems that produce cash flow 24/7.

mentalModels: The Law of Effection (Scale x Magnitude)
Trading Time vs Decoupled Wealth Systems
rules: Shift mindset from pure consumer/employee to producer of scalable software/services.
Never launch a business without high barriers to entry or scalability.
Reinvest income surpluses into compounding assets that generate perpetual cash flow.

title: Coffee Can Investing
author: Saurabh Mukherjea, Rakshit Ranjan and Pranab Uniyal
part: Part 03: Indian Finance, Banking, Taxation and Insurance
thesis: Buy clean Indian compounding machines (ROCE >15% + Revenue >10% for 10 years), eliminate churn, hold for a decade.

chapters.name: The Coffee Can Philosophy
chapters.detail: Originating from Robert Kirby (1984): Buy high-quality compounding machines, put them in a coffee can, and forget about them for 10 years.

chapters.name: The Filtering Criteria
chapters.detail: Revenue growth >10% per annum + Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) >15% every single year for 10 continuous years.

chapters.name: Corporate Governance & Accounting Traps
chapters.detail: How Indian promoters cook books and siphon capital: avoiding value traps and debt-laden businesses.

chapters.name: The Cost of Portfolio Churn
chapters.detail: Brokerage fees, short-term capital gains tax, and timing errors destroy 5-7% of annual returns. Low turnover is the ultimate secret.

mentalModels: The Coffee Can Moat Filter (ROCE >15% + Revenue >10%)
The Power of Inactivity (Patience as a competitive edge)
rules: Build a core equity portfolio of pristine Indian compounding machines (Asian Paints, Titan, HDFC Bank, TCS, Pidilite).
Never sell a Coffee Can stock because of short-term quarterly noise or macroeconomic panic.
Reinvest all dividends to harness explosive long-term compounding.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
part: Part 18: Career Capital, Productivity and Execution
thesis: Intense, uninterrupted focus is the superpower of the modern knowledge economy. Eliminate attention residue.

chapters.name: The Deep Work Hypothesis
chapters.detail: To thrive in the new economy you need: (1) The ability to quickly master hard things, (2) The ability to produce at an elite level, in both quality and speed.

chapters.name: High-Quality Work Formula
chapters.detail: Work Accomplished = Time Spent x Intensity of Focus. Multitasking leaves attention residue that cripples cognitive output.

chapters.name: The 4 Deep Work Philosophies
chapters.detail: Monastic, Bimodal, Rhythmic, and Journalistic scheduling: choose the rhythm that fits your career.

chapters.name: Embracing Boredom & Quitting Social Media
chapters.detail: Training the brain to resist instant dopamine hits and maintain sustained concentration.

rules: Schedule 2-4 hours of uninterrupted deep coding or study daily with zero notifications.
Eliminate phone checks during work intervals to prevent attention residue.
Execute a formal end-of-day shutdown ritual to disconnect and recharge cognitive stamina.

title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
author: Charles T. Munger
thesis: Build a multidisciplinary latticework of mental models; invert, stay in your circle of competence, manage incentives.

chapters.name: The Latticework of Mental Models
chapters.detail: You must know the big ideas in the big disciplines and have them in your mind to make a system that you can use automatically. To a man with only a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.

chapters.name: Inversion ('Invert, Always Invert')
chapters.detail: Instead of asking how to succeed, ask: 'What will guarantee failure?' and systematically avoid those things.

chapters.name: The Psychology of Human Misjudgment
chapters.detail: The 25 cognitive tendencies that lead to catastrophic errors (Reward/Punishment bias, Consistency bias, Social Proof, Lollapalooza effect).

chapters.name: Circle of Competence
chapters.detail: Knowing the boundary of what you understand and refusing to step outside it. It is not how big your circle is; it is knowing where the perimeter lies.

rules: When evaluating an investment or life decision, invert: write down all the ways it can ruin you and avoid them.
Stay strictly within your circle of competence in business and investing.
Study human psychology to recognize when you and others are being blinded by incentives.
